name: application-event-log-table
title: Event Log Table
description: Timestamped analytics event table with a type icon and an expandable JSON payload row, driven by a typed rows prop contract.
useWhen: Displaying a stream of discrete analytics or audit events (signups, payments, webhook calls) with timestamps.
Each event has a structured payload that's useful for debugging but shouldn't clutter the default row.
Events fall into a small set of types (success, info, error) that benefit from an at-a-glance icon.
avoidWhen: You need a continuous scrolling log stream with severity filters — use the Log Viewer component instead.
Events have no structured payload worth expanding — a plain table row is simpler.
Real-time streaming updates are required — pair this with your own live-data subscription, this component is presentation-only.
responsiveBehavior: The table scrolls horizontally on narrow viewports via its wrapping overflow container; the expanded payload row spans the full column width via colSpan regardless of screen size.
accessibility: The expand/collapse toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and a descriptive aria-label naming the event.
Event type icons sit inside a colored badge that is supplementary — the event name itself remains the primary identifier, not color alone.
The JSON payload renders inside a <pre> element so whitespace and formatting are preserved for screen readers and sighted users alike.

variants.title: Event Log Table
variants.description: Event table with a type-coded icon per row, an expand toggle revealing a formatted JSON payload, and a timestamp column.
accessibility: The toggle button's aria-expanded and aria-label stay in sync so the collapsed/expanded state is always announced accurately.

variants.title: Event Log Table (Dark)
variants.description: Event log table adapted for dark surfaces with the same type-icon, expand-toggle, and payload structure.
accessibility: Type-badge colors, event name text, and payload syntax coloring must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
